subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nanoscale LEDs
description: A fast breakdown of Nanoscale LEDs for builders.

hook.text: A single quantum dot emits one photon at a time — the world's smallest LED is just a few nanometers wide.

buildup.text: Quantum dot LEDs sandwich a thin layer of QDs between charge transport layers — electrons and holes recombine in the dots.

discovery.text: QD-LEDs produce pure, saturated colors — each dot size gives a narrow emission peak, better than any phosphor.

twist.text: Blue QD-LEDs degrade fastest — the high-energy photons damage the organic layers around the quantum dots.

climax.text: Samsung's QLED TVs use quantum dots for color — full QD-LED displays without backlights are coming next.

punchline.text: A dot a few nanometers wide outshines a bulb in color purity.

quiz.question: Why do quantum dot LEDs produce purer colors than traditional LEDs?
options: Each dot size emits a narrow, tunable wavelength peak instead of broad-spectrum light
They reflect unwanted wavelengths more efficiently
